correctness.rationale: Conditioned on the driving Brownian environment, the linear SDE integrates to N(M_t,V_t) with M_t=x0 exp[−at−λ∫_0^t|B_s|^p ds], V_t=2D∫_0^t exp[−2au−2λ∫_{t−u}^t|B_s|^p ds]du. Brownian scaling identifies t^{p/2}V_t with an endpoint Laplace integral T=t^{1+p/2}. For any continuous f≥0 with f(1)>0, endpoint DCT gives 2D∫ exp[−2λT∫_{1−y/T}^1 f]dy →D/(λ f(1)), and the tail outside the endpoint neighborhood is bounded by T e^{−cT}; B_1≠0 almost surely. M_t t^{p/4}→0, yielding the joint weak limit (G,√(D/λ)Z/|G|^{p/2}). From Pr(|G|<u)∼√(2/π)u, conditioning on |Z| and DCT yields tail constant 2^{1/2+1/p}Γ(1/2+1/p)(D/λ)^{1/p}/π and moment cutoff s<2/p. For p=2, Z/|G| is Cauchy. No assertion of prelimit moment convergence. Independently checked Cauchy p=2 tail coefficient and the limiting conditional variance scaling algebra; inspected original SciPy verifier.
residual_risks: Uniformity as p→0 or p→∞ not claimed; only each fixed p>0 is proved. Weak convergence does not imply convergence of unbounded moments or fixed-distance rare-excursion intensities.

value.rationale: The full scaling family yields a distributional limit with strongly coupled environmental endpoint and a sharp continuum of nonintegrable-moment thresholds. The p=2 Cauchy identification resolves a physically motivated density limit, while p≠2 and the exact tail constants quantify how changing the power of Brownian stiffness changes transport fluctuations. Nonuniform integrability explains finite prelimit versus divergent limit moments. This is more than reporting routine Gaussian-ratio algebra: the endpoint singular Laplace localization in a nonstationary random trap is the substantive step.
residual_risks: The Gaussian ratio identity is classical, and the p=2 central law has been mentioned earlier; value rests on nonstationary joint scaling, entire p>0 family and sharp constants.

limitations: p>0 fixed, λ,D>0, a≥0, deterministic X0 and independent Brownian noises; no pathwise limit, convergence rates or prelimit moment limit. Full identical-model Gupta–Klapp preprint inaccessible, residual originality risk.
